Lemma
[Dirichlet integral bound for quasiconformal maps]1. ch16:16.13\group chapter-16 Suppose $\varphi :\Gscr \to \Tscr $ is $(K,K')$-quasiconformal and $C^1$. Then

\begin{equation} \tag {16.80} \D (R/2; Y) \le C \end{equation}

where $C=C(\Lambda _0,K,K'R^2,\Lambda _1)$.

Proof

\sketch For regular radii, Stokes’ theorem gives

\begin{equation} \int _{\mathcal S_\rho }J(\varphi )\, dA =\sum _{j=1}^{n(\rho )}\int _{\Gamma _\rho ^{(j)}} (\omega _i\circ \varphi )\frac{d\varphi _i}{ds}\, ds. \tag {16.81} \end{equation}

Together with (16.70), (16.76), and coarea (16.77), this bounds the Dirichlet integral by a product of radial derivatives. Introduce the augmented functions $g=f+\rho R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal D+\rho /R$; the resulting inequality is

\begin{equation} -\frac d{d\rho }\left(\frac1{\mathcal E(\rho )}\right) \ge \frac1{Cg'(\rho )}. \tag {16.82} \end{equation}

Hölder’s inequality on $(R/2,3R/4)$ and (16.79) then give (16.80).

□
